history.new: Cusenza et al. (2022) give the exact length only for n = F_k - 1 (their Thm 1.4) and a bound otherwise; Cheigh et al. (2025) state that a closed form for non-Fibonacci inputs is open and describe the Fibonacci case as treated by Cusenza et al., whose paper we read in full and which treats F_k - 1, not F_k. The sequence L(F_k) is not in the OEIS (EXP-C19-04). Medium-low confidence that no formula exists in the literature. Confirmed 2026-10-19: Cusenza et al. (arXiv:2009.09510) contain no formula for n = F_k; no later Zeckendorf-game paper treats it (arXiv to 2026-10-07); L(F_k) is still not in the OEIS (Historian audit 2026-10-19, reviews/historian_C11_C20.md).

statement:
With F_1 = 1, F_2 = 2, F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}, the longest Zeckendorf game on n = F_k has length
F_{k+2} - k - 2 - floor((k-1)^2/4) (0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 37, 67, 117, 201, ...), i.e. its deficit to the bound
B(F_k) is the quarter-square floor((k-1)^2/4).
title: Closed form of the longest game on a Fibonacci number: L(F_k) = F_{k+2} - k - 2 - floor((k-1)^2/4)
